results.cause: Likely cause: Save on sales invoice:new returns a visible validation error with no field identified in the events (609:e687 and 671:e750 after clicks 608 and 669), and the user edits Customer (612, 614, 638) and Payment Due Date (674, 676) between attempts, so the error is probably tied to a required field that is not clearly pointed out at the point of failure.
results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new screen, when the Save button's validation fails, move focus to the first invalid field (for example Customer or Payment Due Date) and place its error message next to that field, instead of only showing a generic visible error block.

results.cause: Likely cause: a visible validation error appears on the sales invoice:new form after Save is clicked, and the same error also appears when Payment Due Date receives input before any Save click, so the Payment Due Date field is the likely trigger; users then edit Customer and Payment Due Date and click Save again (S0d948c20: events 600, 601:e617, 662, 664:e689 with edits at 668 and 666; S1ff222ed: events 611, 612:e657, 673, 675:e726 with edits at 618 and 680).
results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new screen, when Save is clicked with an invalid form, scroll to and focus the first invalid input and render its message directly beneath that input (for example under Payment Due Date), instead of a generic error that does not identify the field; also check the Payment Due Date validation rule so it does not flag the value on first input.

results.cause: Likely cause: on sales invoice:new, clicking Save repeatedly produces a visible validation error (602:e630, 664:e693) with no field identified in the event data, and the user then returns to Customer (605, 607) and Payment Due Date (666, 668) before the next Save click (662), which suggests the error does not point to the field that failed.
results.fix: Fix: on the sales invoice:new Save button, when validation fails, move focus and scroll to the first invalid field (Customer or Payment Due Date) and show its specific message inline beside that field, rather than only showing a generic visible error.

results.cause: Likely cause: on sales invoice:new, a visible validation error appears about 250-370 ms after the first edit to Payment Due Date in all three sessions, and each Save click then raises another visible error. Users return to Payment Due Date after the last error, edit it again, and leave the screen without a further Save click (S4f6ead43 navigates to customer:list; Se8131012 navigates after a Back click; Sab8e6b94 shows no save after the last edit within its window).
results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new form, render the Payment Due Date validation message inline beneath that input with the specific rule it breaks (for example, the date must be on or after the invoice date), clear that message as soon as the value changes, and make the Save error summary name the offending field so it links back to Payment Due Date.

results.cause: Likely cause: in session S4f6ead43, each Save click (599 at 12457 ms, 661 at 14374 ms) is followed within about 5-8 ms by a visible validation error (600:e623, 663:e689), and the edits made between attempts (Customer 604/606, Payment Due Date 665/667) are not followed by a cleared error. This suggests Save validates a field the user did not change, possibly Warehouse, which received focus (580) with no input_activity before the first Save.
results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new Save button handler, when validation fails, move focus to the first invalid field (for example the Warehouse combobox) and show its error message inline beside that field, instead of the generic visible error that appears at the top of the form.

results.cause: Likely cause: the Apply button on sales invoice:new gives no observable response after the first click. Five clicks land at the same spot within about 1 s (events 279, 284, 287, 291, 294), and no navigation, overlay, or error event appears between them, so the user appears to repeat the click while waiting for a result.
results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new "Apply" button, disable the button and show a pending indicator as soon as the first click fires, and keep it disabled until the apply handler resolves, so repeated clicks are ignored and the user sees that the action is in progress.

results.cause: Likely cause: the Apply button on sales invoice:new gives no recorded response after a click, so users click it again at the same spot. In all three sessions, five clicks on Apply (279, 283, 287, 290, 294 in Sabc305a8; 279, 284, 287, 290, 294 in S3c997a45; 289, 294, 298, 301, 305 in S3edf7344) occur within about 1 s with no navigation, overlay, dialog, or error event in between.
results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new screen, change the Apply button (the button at about x 1375–1400, y 850–875, in the Taxes Section) so that a first click immediately disables it and shows a pending state until the apply action completes, and show a visible confirmation or updated taxes totals when it finishes.

results.cause: Likely cause: the Apply button on sales invoice:new gives no visible response after the first click, since no navigation, overlay, or error event follows the repeated Apply clicks (279, 283, 287, 290, 294 in S806b5d05; 279, 284, 287, 291, 294 in S3a99876d; 280, 285, 288, 292, 295 in Sf6922579), so users click again at nearly the same spot.
results.fix: Fix: On the Apply button in the sales invoice:new Taxes Section, disable the button and show a pending/spinner state immediately on the first click, and re-enable it only when the tax update finishes, so repeat clicks are blocked and the response is visible.

results.cause: Likely cause: on the Item (list) screen, users scroll the list repeatedly (scroll events on "Item 190" up to 7850 px) and then click the "Item 190" row, which is followed about 100-150 ms later by a navigation back to accounts receivable:report, so the list row appears to route back to the report instead of staying on the item. A console error also fires within about 200-300 ms of arriving on Item (list) in all three sessions.
results.fix: Fix: on the Item (list) screen, change the "Item 190" row click handler (the div at about x 1250-1300, y 250-275) so it opens the item rather than navigating to accounts receivable:report, and fix the console error thrown when item:list mounts so the list renders without the brief overlay.

results.cause: Likely cause: on item:list, the scroll region labelled "Item 190" is long (page extent at least 8762 px) and has no in-list search or filter, so users scroll it back and forth with the pointer held at about (1275, 400) and no clicks until they reach a target row, as the repeated scroll_y reversals (for example 1800, 3600, 2950, 5150, 4250, 6850, 6050, 7850) in each session show.
results.fix: Fix: On the item:list screen, add a search/filter input above the scrollable list container (the element labelled "Item 190" and its sibling rows) that narrows rows by item name or code, so users can reach a row without scrolling more than about 12 screens.

results.cause: Likely cause: clicking the "Item 190" row on the Item (list) screen navigates straight back to Accounts Receivable (report), about 150 ms after the click, in all three sessions, so the row click appears to route to the report instead of an item view.
results.fix: Fix: On the Item (list) screen, check the click handler or link target on the list row element (the "Item 190" row at about x=1250, y=275) and make it open that item's detail view instead of returning to the accounts receivable report route.

results.cause: Likely cause: On item:list, the Item 190 scroll container has no visible way to reach a target row quickly, so users scroll down and back up in repeated passes with no clicks in between, then click Item 190 near the top of the list.
results.fix: Fix: On the item:list screen, add a search or filter input above the Item 190 list container so users can jump to the target row, and check that the pointer region at about (1275, 400) inside that container is not a non-interactive element that users are trying to use as a scroll handle.

results.cause: Likely cause: every arrival on Customer (list) logs a console error and briefly shows a three-part overlay that is removed within about 15 to 30 ms, and users go back to Sales Invoice (new) about 2 s later, so the list page may not be giving them a usable result on arrival, though the events do not show what they did there.
results.fix: Fix: On the Customer (list) screen, resolve the console error logged on each load and stop the loading overlay from flashing, then check whether the Customer combobox on Sales Invoice (new) can open a customer picker in place instead of a full navigation to Customer (list).

results.cause: Likely cause: On Sales Invoice (new), a tab or link control near the top-left (about x=125, y=100) appears to route to customer:list, and each return to sales invoice:new is followed by a loading overlay and a console error, so users re-open the invoice screen during one task.
results.fix: Fix: On the Sales Invoice (new) screen, change the top-left tab/link at about (125,100) that navigates to customer:list so it does not unmount the form, for example by opening the customer list in a side panel or new tab, or by keeping the draft state across the route change.

results.cause: Likely cause: a role=tab button on Sales Invoice (new) appears to route the user to Customer (list), because each round trip starts 1.3–2.3 s after a tab-button focus (271 before the first trip in Sc39bbfef, 549 before the second; 272 and 548 in the other sessions) and the return to Sales Invoice (new) follows about 2 s later (app:2, app:4).
results.fix: Fix: On the Sales Invoice (new) screen, identify the role=tab button that is focused just before each navigation to Customer (list) and stop it from navigating away; if it is meant to pick a customer, render that picker inline on the form instead of routing to the Customer list.

results.cause: Likely cause: On sales invoice:new, the first click on the Effective Value Date input does not seem to start text entry. In all three windows the user clicks the field, then clicks it again about 4–5 s later, and the first keystroke follows that second click within 15–23 ms.
results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new screen, check the focus and click handlers on the Effective Value Date input (for example, a date picker that opens or closes on focus or click) so that one click leaves the input focused and accepting keystrokes; then confirm in a test that a single click followed by typing produces input_activity without a second click.

results.cause: Likely cause: On purchase order:new, a blocking coverage overlay appears about 6 ms after Save is clicked and is removed about 6 s later in all three sessions, with no visible, console or exception errors in that window, which suggests the Save step holds the screen until its work completes.
results.fix: Fix: On the purchase order:new screen, change the Save button's click handler so it shows an inline loading state on the Save button and does not raise the full-screen overlay, and instrument the save call it waits on to find out why it takes about 6 s.

results.cause: Likely cause: clicking Save on the purchase order:new screen shows a full-screen overlay right away and keeps it for about 15 s with no visible error or progress indicator in the windows, so the user has no feedback while the save runs and then clicks Save again.
results.fix: Fix: on the purchase order:new screen, change the Save button's click handler so it disables the button and shows an inline spinner on the Save button instead of the blocking full-screen overlay, and log the save request's duration to find out why it takes about 15 s.

results.cause: Likely cause: on Sales Invoice (list), a console error fires about 0.3 s after the screen loads, and the app then navigates back to Sales Invoice (new) about 2 s later with no user click in between, which suggests an automatic or error-driven return rather than a user choice.
results.fix: Fix: On the Sales Invoice (list) screen, check the load handler that runs right after the console error and remove or guard any programmatic navigation back to Sales Invoice (new), so the list stays on screen.

results.fix: Fix: On the sales invoice:new screen, change the "Items" label/tab control near (450, 600) so it switches to the items section in place instead of navigating to customer:list, or, if it must leave the form, save the draft or show an unsaved-changes prompt before the route change.
